title: The Tailor, the Lady, and the Guard
summary: In Cairo lived an industrious tailor named Marwan and his devoted wife, Dalal. Marwan was celebrated for his impeccable sewing, crafting robes for noblemen and commoners alike.
keywords: the tailor and the lady and the captain
full_text:
In Cairo lived an industrious tailor named Marwan and his devoted wife, Dalal. Marwan was celebrated for his impeccable sewing, crafting robes for noblemen and commoners alike.

An arrogant captain of the Citadel guard, strutting past the tailor's shop window, took a fancy to Dalal and resolved to displace the humble tailor.
He strode into the workshop, threw down three bolts of heavy gold-threaded damask, and demanded haughtily:
'Tailor, sew me five ceremonial coats from this cloth by tomorrow noon. If a single seam is crooked, or if thou art late by one minute, I shall have thy shop closed and confiscate thy goods!'

Marwan worked through the night, but realizing the impossible timeline, grew exhausted.
Dalal stepped forward: 'Husband, let me cut and baste the linings while thou sewest the outer seams.'

Working in harmony with swift, practiced fingers, the husband and wife completed all five coats before dawn, stitching them with absolute perfection.
However, Dalal noticed that inside each collar, the arrogant captain had requested an embroidered phrase praising his own valor.

Dalal cleverly altered the embroidery with minute gold stitches. Instead of 'The Invincible Captain', the delicate letters read: 'Patience and Modesty are the Crown of the Brave.'

When the Captain arrived at noon, expecting to find the tailor exhausted and behind schedule, he was astonished to see five magnificent coats laid out in flawless order.
When he inspected the collar and read the subtle moral reminder, his face flushed.
The Captain looked at the united, dignified couple standing quietly before him with clear eyes and honest hands.

His arrogance melted into respect.
'Tailor,' he admitted, 'thou and thy wife have outworked my haste and outwitted my pride. The work is worthy of an emperor.'
He paid Marwan double the agreed price, apologized for his roughness, and became a lifelong patron and protector of the workshop, proving that collaborative diligence and moral dignity command genuine respect.
moral: Honest industry and fidelity safeguard a home against intrusive pride.
